chapter: Los Angeles nightlife: Sheffield, Hamp and the Cotton Club
title: Lionel Hampton as a young drummer; jam sessions at Nat Moore's
summary: Joe recalls young Hamp as a top drummer playing two-finger piano at jam sessions in Nat Moore's house and the Crawfish Inn.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You were saying about Hamp, you thought Hamp might have been playing with the band. I know when he first started his career, he started playing with Andrew Blake,
Darensbourg - 177
didn't he?

blake sent for him. I don't know how Blake got to know him. But the first... I had seen Hamp... Well, I've seen pictures. Blake had that picture taken in Chicago with him and Hamp maybe 14 or 15 years old. Did you see that picture?
Yeah, I saw that picture.
He had the cap on. But I didn't know him then. But maybe Blake had something to do with him coming to Los Angeles, for that matter, too.
But did you know Hamp out here when he first started?
Oh, yes.
Did you ever play with him when he was starting out?

Oh, yes, I played with him! We used to have jam sessions at a place called Nat Moore's, a great big old house that all the musicians went around. It was a place on Naomi Street in Los Angeles, right off of 12th and Central. And they had another place that we used to congregate and play called the Crawfish Inn.
Where was that?
That was on Hooper Avenue in Los Angeles. And those were all-night joints; it went all night long.
Darensbourg - 178
And we'd somehow be in Nat Moore, and then that was the first time I...
Hamp?
Hamp was playing the two-fingered piano. One time we had been playing, and he got up from the drums, and the first tune I remember him playing... He used to play "Chinatown." [SINGS REFRAIN]
He did it with two fingers?
He used two fingers.
Was he much of a drummer in those early days?
Oh, he was one of your top drummers.
Oh really. He was that good.
